claim.summary: For a nonempty finite multiset R with Phi(s) = sum m_rho/(s - rho): all Re rho <= sigma_0 iff Re Phi > 0 on Re s > sigma_0. For real points Gamma and one conjugate pair gamma +- i delta of multiplicity m, the Laguerre expression L(x) = sum m_w/(x - w)^2 on the real line is negative at x = gamma iff sum over Gamma of m'/(gamma - gamma')^2 < 2m/delta^2, the pair's term is at least -2m/delta^2 and negative only for |x - gamma| < delta, and L >= 0 everywhere when the real points have gaps at most 2 delta/sqrt(m) covering (gamma - delta, gamma + delta).
claim.assessment: Working elementary proofs. The half-plane sign criterion is equivalent to the zero-free statement at every boundary, so it is not a weaker premise; the local real-line (Laguerre, phase-monotonicity) condition cannot fail for an off-line pair farther from the line than half the gap of the real points around it times sqrt(m), while the global count of real zeros detects every pair and is the goal's statement. Finite configurations only; part (a) is the finite model of a known equivalence and no novelty is claimed; the general Hermite-Biehler and de Branges sources are not read.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Shows for finite configurations that the Hermite-Biehler lead's two natural forms are the goal's statement and a criterion blind in the relevant range.
significance.next_action: Read a source on structure functions of de Branges type for xi and state which condition is equivalent to the goal and what is known unconditionally.

claim.summary: Complete-grid Gram model, one off-axis pair of multiplicity m at distance delta and any real points, G = G_on + B: m(kappa+1) <= lambda_max(G) <= m(kappa+1) + lambda_max(G_on) and -m(kappa-1) <= lambda_min(G) <= min(0, -m(kappa-1) + eta), eta = e_y^T G_on e_y <= lambda_max(G_on); flat window: lambda_max(G_on) <= M_loc(3 + (2/pi)(1 + ln K)). So an operator-norm bound B at bandwidth Lam gives delta <= (log B + log(4 delta Lam))/Lam for a solitary pair with delta Lam >= 1, and a one-sided bound lambda_min >= -B the same with B + 1 + eta.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof (test vectors e_x, e_y and Weyl). A small refinement of solitary amplification, whose part 4 already has the lower bound for lambda_max; added is the upper bound for lambda_min with its margin, and the observation that the extreme eigenvalues, unlike the second moment, see a solitary pair once kappa exceeds the on-line part's size, also at bandwidth log T. Complete grid only; the cut grid is not treated. The premise (an eigenvalue bound of size T^eps for the import's form) is not available, follows from the goal in the model, and is expected to be a local restatement of it.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Replaces the earlier reading that the Gram mechanism needs bandwidth beyond log T, which holds for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm only; names the premise at the import's own bandwidth.
significance.next_action: Derive the prime side of the quadratic form at bandwidth log T from the import's explicit formula and state which sum over prime powers bounds the extreme eigenvalues.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry for every window (the on-line bound for the flat window); control on 18 configurations, including real points denser than the grid.

relationships.note: Refines solitary amplification (adds the upper bound for lambda_max and both bounds for lambda_min); uses the pair atom spectrum and the real configuration bound. The Gram form's prime side as a weighted square integral: new relationship with lem:prime-side-form-bound. Sign criteria for the logarithmic derivative of a finite configuration: new relationship with prop:log-derivative-sign-criteria.

relationships.scope: The local real-line condition can fail only for pairs nearer than the local gap; the Gram form's extreme eigenvalues are proved to see pairs farther than about loglog T/log T; between the scales neither gives detection.
